title: Offering Help
subtitle: How to offer assistance and respond to customer concerns
description: Learn the phrases sales professionals use to offer help, respond to concerns, and keep the conversation moving — 'Can I help you?', 'Do you need help with…?', 'Don't hesitate to contact me.'
dialogueSubtitle: Riley follows up with Dana after her first week on the Brightline trial

vocabulary.definition: To help someone with a task or problem.
vocabulary.example: Is there anything else I can assist you with before we finish the call?

vocabulary.definition: Free and ready to help; not currently busy.
vocabulary.example: I'm available this afternoon if you'd like to go through it together.

vocabulary.definition: A worry or question someone wants to discuss.
vocabulary.example: Do you have any concerns about the setup that I can help with?

vocabulary.definition: To plan or set up something in advance.
vocabulary.example: I can arrange a call with our onboarding team for later today.

vocabulary.definition: To pause before doing something, often because you are unsure.
vocabulary.example: Please don't hesitate to contact me if anything is urgent.

vocabulary.definition: To put someone in touch with another person who can help.
vocabulary.example: Let me connect you with Carlos — he handles all new customer setups.

vocabulary.definition: To explain something so it is easier to understand.
vocabulary.example: Can I clarify how the billing works? I want to make sure it is clear.
If anything is urgent, please contact me directly and I will respond the same day.

phrasalVerbs.definition: The standard opening phrase to offer help at the start of a conversation.
phrasalVerbs.example: Hi Dana — can I help you with anything today?

phrasalVerbs.definition: Ask if someone needs assistance with a specific task or problem.
phrasalVerbs.example: Do you need help with setting up the dashboard for your team?

phrasalVerbs.definition: A slightly more formal way to offer help.
phrasalVerbs.example: How can I assist you today — is it about the billing or the setup?

phrasalVerbs.definition: Invite someone to contact you if a situation changes or if they need anything.
phrasalVerbs.example: Let me know if you have any questions after the call — I'm happy to help.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Encourage someone to ask for help without worrying about bothering you.
phrasalVerbs.example: Don't hesitate to call me if anything comes up — that's what I'm here for.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Check if a customer needs more help before ending a conversation.
phrasalVerbs.example: Is there anything else I can help you with before we finish?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Hi Dana — it's Riley from Brightline. Can I help you with anything? I wanted to check in after your first week on the trial.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Perfect timing, actually. I have a few [[concern:a worry or question someone wants to discuss]]s about the dashboard setup.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Of course — I'm [[available:free and ready to help; not currently busy]] right now if you'd like to go through it together. Or I can [[arrange:to plan or set up something in advance]] a call with our onboarding team.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: A call with your team would be great. Can you [[connect:to put someone in touch with another person who can help]] me with someone today?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Let me connect you with Carlos — he handles all new customer setups. Do you need help with anything else before I do?

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Yes, actually. Can you [[clarify:to explain something so it is easier to understand]] how the annual billing works? I wasn't sure I understood it correctly.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Of course. If you pay annually, the monthly rate works out at $124 instead of $149 — a saving of $25 a month. Does that help?

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Yes, that's much clearer. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Great. And please don't [[hesitate:to pause before doing something, often because you are unsure]] to contact me directly if anything is [[urgent:needing attention quickly; cannot wait]]. I'm here to help.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: I will. I really appreciate it.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Is there anything else I can [[assist:to help someone with a task or problem]] you with before I connect you to Carlos?

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: No, I think that covers everything for now.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the customer's line, then discuss which response (A, B, or C) is best. Choose your answer together, then click to see if you were right — and why.

items.customerLine: I'm not sure how to get started.
options: Don't worry — most people find it easy once they start.
Check the help section on our website — everything is explained there.
Let me know what you need and I can assist you directly, or I can arrange a call with our onboarding team.
items.explanation: C is correct. It offers two clear, personal options and shows you are ready to help right now. A is dismissive and doesn't actually help. B sends the customer away instead of offering direct support.

items.customerLine: I have a question about the invoice I received.
options: Can you send it to me and I will clarify it for you right away?
Invoices are handled by our finance team — I will have to pass you on.
What is the question? I will try my best to answer it.
items.explanation: A is correct. It offers direct, personal help and a clear next step. B is unnecessarily bureaucratic — most invoice questions can be handled without passing the customer elsewhere. C sounds hesitant before you have even started.

items.customerLine: There might be a problem with my account.
options: That shouldn't happen — are you sure you're doing it correctly?
I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more? I can help or connect you with our support team right now.
You can submit a support ticket and someone will get back to you within 48 hours.
items.explanation: B is correct. It shows empathy, asks for more information, and offers a direct path to help. A is condescending and will upset the customer. C is the slowest possible solution and feels impersonal.

items.customerLine: I'm busy right now — can we talk later?
options: Sure — just let me know when you are free.
Of course. I'm available this afternoon or tomorrow morning — which works better for you?
No problem — I'll try to call you again next week.
items.explanation: B is correct. It offers two specific options right away, which makes it easy for the customer to say yes. A is too vague — the customer has to do all the work. C assumes a timeline without asking and may be too far away.

profileMatch.instructions: Read each customer situation. As a group, decide which type of support is best for them — a self-service guide, an onboarding call, or a dedicated account manager. Use phrases from this lesson like 'I can arrange…' and 'Let me connect you with…' to explain your choices. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: Felix
profiles.description: Felix set up the tool himself and just has a quick question about one feature. He's busy and doesn't want a meeting — he just wants a fast answer he can act on immediately.

profiles.name: Mia
profiles.description: Mia's 20-person team is starting their trial next week. She needs someone to walk her team through the key features live and answer questions as they come up. A document won't be enough.

profiles.name: Alex
profiles.description: Alex's company is running a critical operation on Brightline. When something is urgent, he needs to reach a real person immediately — not wait in a queue or search a help centre. He needs a direct line.

options.label: Self-service guide
options.description: A written step-by-step guide and short video walkthrough. Available 24/7 and covers the most common questions. Best for customers who are confident and just need a quick reference.

options.label: Onboarding call
options.description: A live 45-minute call with a Brightline specialist who walks the team through the platform and answers questions in real time. Best for teams who are new and want a structured start.

options.label: Dedicated account manager
options.description: A named contact who is always available by phone or message. They know the customer's setup, can arrange urgent calls at short notice, and handle any concerns directly. Best for large or critical accounts.

finishTheLine.instructions: The salesperson's line has been cut off. As a group, discuss how you would finish it. Try to use phrases from this lesson like 'Don't hesitate to…', 'I can arrange…', or 'Let me connect you with…'. There is no single correct answer — compare your ideas, then click to see one possible answer.
